data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'panchaja' meaning 'fifth'. In Hindu mythology, the god Krishna is also called 'Pankaj' as he is the fifth avatar of Lord Vishnu. The name symbolizes the divine and the precious. The name पंकज carries the meaning “Jewel, Ornament” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose पंकज usually hope their child will grow to embody jewel, ornament and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'पंकज' (Pankaj) is of significant cultural importance in Hinduism as it is associated with the god Krishna, one of the most revered deities in Hindu mythology. Being the fifth avatar of Lord Vishnu, Krishna's name 'पंकज' highlights his distinctive place in the divine pantheon.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name 'पंकज' (Pankaj) represents the divine and the precious. It is a reminder of the precious nature of every individual soul, which is a reflection of the divine and is treated as such in Hinduism. The name also symbolizes the sweetness and grace of God Krishna, who is considered to be an embodiment of love, joy, and spiritual beauty.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name 'पंकज' (Pankaj) is believed to originate from the Sanskrit word 'पंक' (pank), meaning 'five' and 'ज' (j), signifying 'knowledge'. Thus, Pankaj symbolizes one who possesses profound knowledge or wisdom of the five fundamental elements of nature.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to the name 'Pandu' can be found in the Puranic text Harivamsa. Here, Pandu is described as the son of King Yayati and his wife Devayani. The name 'Pandu' in this context is believed to mean 'painted' or 'adorned', possibly due to his connection to the god Indra who blessed him with his divine powers.
historical_references.context: Harivamsa, a Hindu scripture that forms part of the Indian epic Mahabharata, provides additional details about the early history of the Pandava dynasty.
